headline: “Targeting Yellow Journalism, Not Honest Media”—Dr. Enayetullah Abbasi’s Stance Clarified Amid Irrelevant Legal Notice
standfirst: Supporters and conscious citizens have strongly protested the misinformation and legal notice directed at renowned Islamic scholar and speaker Dr. Sayed Muhammad Enayetullah Abbasi.
keyPoints: Supporters say Dr. Abbasi’s remarks were aimed at “yellow journalists”, not objective, professional journalists.
The remarks were made at an annual Islamic conference on October 19 at Nishchintapur Hafizia Madrasa in Matlab, Chandpur.

paragraphs: Supporters and conscious citizens have strongly protested the misinformation and legal notice directed at renowned Islamic scholar and speaker Dr. Sayed Muhammad Enayetullah Abbasi. They clarified that his recent statements were in no way aimed at objective, professional journalists, but were strictly intended to unmask "yellow journalists" who spread negative framing and work against national interests.

The controversy stems from an annual Islamic conference on October 19 at Nishchintapur Hafizia Madrasa in Matlab, Chandpur. Addressing the gathering, Dr. Abbasi highlighted how a section of unethical reporting undermines genuine positive efforts in the country.

sections.heading: What he said
paragraphs: "A young official holding the responsibility of a state minister led his team to break down the chain of a drug syndicate. But instead of highlighting this positive achievement, certain media outlets focused negatively, reporting that he ran around with a pistol. These individuals are not journalists; they are hazardous. They practice yellow journalism, run on funds from foreign intelligence agencies, and do not wish to see Bangladesh prosper."

Supporters and analysts emphasize that Dr. Abbasi’s critique was directed specifically at biased media figures who gloss over noble actions—such as dismantling drug syndicates—to fabricate sensationalized, negative narratives. His remarks targeted those allegedly influenced by foreign agendas, rather than the mainstream journalism community as a whole.

sections.heading: Context on the legal notice
paragraphs: Following the event, a legal notice was served on behalf of Azharul Islam Sujon, an executive member of the Court Reporters Unit, through Supreme Court Advocate Khademul Islam. The notice alleged that Dr. Abbasi’s remarks defamed journalists and created an intimidating environment for the profession.

However, observers and supporters argue that the allegations in the notice are unfounded and lack logical standing. They maintain that Dr. Abbasi was expressing public indignation toward corrupt and sensationalist reporting. Rather than threatening professional media, his speech called out unethical elements whose actions undermine genuine news reporting and social progress.

socialSummary: Supporters say Dr. Enayetullah Abbasi’s remarks targeted “yellow journalism”, not honest media, as they protest a legal notice served over his October 19 speech in Matlab, Chandpur.
